items.c: Theca lutein cysts are functional cysts resulting from high beta-HCG levels, seen in molar pregnancy, multifetal gestation, and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

items.c: The presence of an eccentric scolex within a ring-enhancing brain lesion is pathognomonic for neurocysticercosis.
items.a: Neuroradiology

items.c: Decubitus views are useful in demonstrating air-fluid levels when the patient cannot stand for an erect abdominal film.
items.a: Gastrointestinal

items.c: Subdural hematomas are typically venous in origin and characteristically assume a crescent shape on CT, unlike epidural hematomas which are biconvex.
items.a: Trauma

items.c: The spider web appearance on hepatic venography is pathognomonic for Budd-Chiari syndrome.
items.a: Hepatobiliary

items.c: Greenstick fractures represent incomplete fractures in children where the bone bends and breaks only on the tension side.
items.a: Musculoskeletal

items.c: A mechanical large bowel obstruction can present with secondary small bowel dilation if the ileocaecal valve is incompetent.
items.a: Gastrointestinal

items.c: Paget's disease commonly causes cortical thickening, bowing deformities, and characteristic incomplete cortical fractures.
items.a: Musculoskeletal

items.c: Pilocytic astrocytomas, often associated with NF1, typically present as cystic lesions with a non-enhancing wall and an enhancing mural nodule.
items.a: Neuroradiology

items.c: In a rolling hiatus hernia, the gastro-oesophageal junction remains in its normal anatomical position.
items.a: Rolling hiatus hernia

items.c: Look for the sun-ray appearance and Codman triangle as specific signs of osteosarcoma on imaging.
items.a: Osteosarcoma

items.c: The posterior malleolus is a key component of the distal tibia that must be evaluated on lateral ankle radiographs.
items.a: Posterior malleolus

items.c: Batwing distribution is also known as butterfly shadow, reflecting the distribution of pulmonary oedema.
items.a: Batwing distribution

items.c: Always look for the empty right iliac fossa sign to support a diagnosis of intussusception.
items.a: Intussusception

items.c: Calcified pleural plaques are a key diagnostic clue for asbestos-related disease.
items.a: Asbestosis

items.c: Medial joint space narrowing combined with osteophytes is the classic radiological presentation of knee osteoarthritis.
items.a: Osteoarthritis

items.c: Lipping of the vertebral bodies is a classic degenerative marker seen in cervical spondylosis.
items.a: Cervical spondylosis

items.c: Look for osteophytes and subarticular sclerosis to distinguish degenerative osteoarthritis from inflammatory arthritides like rheumatoid arthritis.
items.a: Osteoarthritis

items.c: Always look for the absence of osteophytes and the presence of erosions to distinguish inflammatory rheumatoid arthritis from degenerative osteoarthritis.
items.a: Rheumatoid arthritis

items.c: Osteochondroma is the most common benign bone tumour.
items.a: Osteochondroma

items.c: The radial head should always point to the capitellum on all views; if it does not, suspect a Monteggia injury.
items.a: Monteggia fracture-dislocation

items.c: Sulcal effacement and transependymal CSF spread are key indicators of raised intracranial pressure in hydrocephalus.
items.a: Transependymal CSF spread

items.c: Ensure the ankle mortice is even throughout when evaluating radiographs for potential fractures.
items.a: Lateral and medial malleolus

items.c: Always check for symmetry of the lateral masses of the atlas relative to the axis on the open mouth view.
items.a: Lateral masses of the Atlas

items.c: ARDS is a non-cardiogenic condition; look for the absence of cardiomegaly on the chest X-ray.
items.a: Bilateral diffuse airspace consolidation

items.c: A sequestrum is a hallmark of chronic osteomyelitis appearing as a dense bone fragment within a lytic lesion.
items.a: Periosteal reaction

items.c: The posterior vertebral line is the most important alignment marker as it is least affected by osteophytes.
items.a: A normal cervical spine

items.c: SDH is crescent-shaped and not limited by sutures.
items.a: Crescent-shaped hyperdensity

items.c: Reduced disc spaces combined with osteophytes are the radiological hallmarks of lumbar spondylosis.
items.a: Lumbar spondylosis

items.c: Bullae are distinguished from pneumothorax by the presence of thin curvilinear walls and lack of a pleural line.
items.a: Giant bullous emphysema

items.c: Always look for bowel loops in the hemithorax when a neonate has respiratory distress and mediastinal shift.
items.a: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia

items.c: The water-lily sign is pathognomonic for a ruptured hydatid cyst where the endocyst membrane collapses into the fluid.
items.a: Water-lily sign

items.c: Skier's thumb is specifically associated with ulnar collateral ligament disruption.
items.a: Skier's thumb

items.c: Tram tracking is a highly specific sign for bronchial wall thickening in bronchiectasis.
items.a: Tram tracking

items.c: The presence of transverse foramina is the most reliable anatomical marker to distinguish a cervical vertebra from other spinal segments.
items.a: Cervical vertebra

items.c: A step deformity of greater than 3mm on a lateral cervical spine X-ray indicates an unstable spine.
items.a: Perched facets

items.c: Consider myoid hamartoma in the differential of a breast mass containing adipose tissue and smooth muscle bundles that stain positive for SMA and desmin.
items.a: Myoid hamartoma

items.c: Always consider pseudoachalasia in patients with a bird's beak appearance if there is rapid symptom progression or atypical features on endoscopy.
items.a: Bird's beak sign

items.t: Perform a bone marrow biopsy and aspirate at a site of focal lesion identified on WB DW-MRI
items.c: Whole-body MRI with diffusion-weighted sequences is the preferred imaging modality for the initial workup and staging of myeloma, offering superior sensitivity for occult focal lesions.
items.a: Perform a bone marrow biopsy and aspirate at a site of focal lesion identified on WB DW-MRI

items.c: Osteofibrous dysplasia is a 'touch-me-not' lesion often managed conservatively, typically occurring in the tibial diaphysis of young children.
items.a: Bone tumours

items.c: Think of Lemierre syndrome in any patient with a recent pharyngitis who develops persistent fever and neck swelling, even if the initial presentation was misdiagnosed as viral.
items.a: Lemierre syndrome

items.c: In a premenopausal woman, the combination of diffuse round pulmonary cysts and a renal or retroperitoneal angiomyolipoma is pathognomonic for lymphangioleiomyomatosis.
items.a: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis

items.c: Atherosclerosis is a common process in patients over 45 years, manifesting as calcified, irregular plaque formation in large and medium-sized arteries.
items.a: Vascular

items.c: Mirror image artefact in the trachea arises from the highly reflective air-mucosa interface, often leading to the false appearance of deeper structures within the tracheal lumen.
items.a: Mirror image artefact

items.c: The Kocher criteria (fever, non-weight bearing, elevated inflammatory markers, leukocytosis) are essential for distinguishing septic arthritis from transient synovitis in children with hip effusions.
items.a: Paediatric Hip

items.t: Cerebrospinal fluid HSV-1 polymerase chain reaction
items.c: In patients with acute confusion and temporal lobe abnormalities on MRI, suspect HSVE and initiate empiric acyclovir before waiting for PCR confirmation.
items.a: Cerebrospinal fluid HSV-1 polymerase chain reaction

items.c: The whirlpool sign on cross-sectional imaging is a high-specificity indicator of mesenteric torsion and midgut volvulus.
items.a: Malrotation with midgut volvulus

items.c: Lateral cortical thickening in the femoral shaft is highly suggestive of bisphosphonate-related fracture.
items.a: Musculoskeletal

items.t: Increased thickness of the pericardium on CT
items.c: Look for pericardial calcification or thickening >4 mm on CT to confirm constrictive pericarditis when clinical signs of right heart failure are present.
items.a: Increased thickness of the pericardium on CT

items.c: Nuchal translucency > 3 mm in the first trimester is a marker for chromosomal abnormalities and requires further evaluation.
items.a: Fetal anomalies

items.c: Scutum erosion and opacification of Prussak's space are the earliest and most common radiological signs of a pars flaccida cholesteatoma.
items.a: Temporal bone

items.t: Coil embolization of the splenic artery proximal and distal to the pseudoaneurysm
items.c: Exclusion of the pseudoaneurysm sac by proximal and distal coil embolization is the gold standard, ensuring no retrograde filling occurs.
items.a: Coil embolization of the splenic artery proximal and distal to the pseudoaneurysm

items.c: A concha bullosa is a common anatomical variant that is typically asymptomatic but can rarely cause nasal obstruction.
items.a: Paranasal sinuses

items.c: Colpocephaly refers to the disproportionate enlargement of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles due to callosal dysgenesis.
items.a: Congenital brain malformations

items.c: A dacryocystocele results from nasolacrimal duct obstruction and may present to the emergency department when secondarily infected as dacryocystitis.
items.a: Nasolacrimal apparatus

items.c: Omental cake is pathognomonic for extensive peritoneal metastatic disease and is most frequently associated with ovarian, gastric, or colon cancer.
items.a: Omental cake

items.c: Plantar fasciitis is usually a clinical diagnosis, but MRI shows thickening and increased T2 signal at the calcaneal insertion.
items.a: Foot

items.c: In patients with acute abdominal pain and unremarkable abdominal imaging, always consider pulmonary embolism, especially if the D-dimer is elevated or there is unexplained tachycardia.
items.a: Pulmonary artery filling defects

items.c: Gastric GISTs frequently present as large, lobulated, submucosal masses with variable intramural, endogastric, or exogastric extension.
items.a: Stomach

items.c: The yolk sac is the earliest structure identified within the gestational sac and should typically be visible when the sac diameter reaches 8 mm.
items.a: Obstetrics

items.c: The bear's paw sign, characterized by multiloculated low-attenuation areas replacing the renal parenchyma, should always raise suspicion for XGP in the context of a staghorn calculus.
items.a: Bear's paw sign

items.c: In a polytrauma patient, symmetric perithyroidal fluid with preserved thyroid morphology is a marker of hypoperfusion rather than direct neck trauma.
items.a: Shock-related thyroid change

items.t: Measurement of serum factor XIII activity
items.c: In spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage with normal routine coagulation panels, always consider factor XIII deficiency.
items.a: Measurement of serum factor XIII activity

items.c: Cor triatriatum sinistrum acts functionally like mitral stenosis and can cause unexplained pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary oedema.
items.a: Congenital heart disease

items.c: In a child with a suprarenal mass, elevated urinary VMA levels should prompt a diagnosis of neuroblastoma regardless of cystic or hemorrhagic imaging appearances.
items.a: Neuroblastoma

items.t: Colloid cyst of the third ventricle
items.c: A midline cystic lesion at the foramen of Monro causing obstructive hydrocephalus should be considered a colloid cyst regardless of atypical signal characteristics.
items.a: Colloid cyst of the third ventricle

items.c: The presence of a bladder-base filling defect in a female infant should raise immediate suspicion for a duplex system with an ectopic ureterocele.
items.a: Ureterocele with duplex kidney

items.c: Always consider VACTERL association when esophageal atresia is identified on a chest radiograph.
items.a: Paediatric

items.c: Langerhans cell histiocytosis should be considered in children presenting with unexplained lytic bone lesions and soft tissue swellings.
items.a: Langerhans cell histiocytosis

items.c: The presence of fluid-fluid levels on MRI in a bone lesion is highly suggestive of an aneurysmal bone cyst, but one must always exclude telangiectatic osteosarcoma.
items.a: Fluid-fluid levels

items.c: In elderly patients with unexplained right heart failure and right-sided volume overload, always consider PAPVR with an associated sinus venosus ASD despite negative initial echocardiography.
items.a: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return

items.c: Porcelain gallbladder is no longer considered an absolute indication for radical resection, and laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the preferred management.
items.a: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy

items.c: In infants with five or more cutaneous hemangiomas, screening abdominal ultrasound is mandatory to exclude visceral involvement, specifically IHH.
items.a: Infantile hepatic haemangioma

items.c: Incomplete resection of the coccyx during surgery for sacrococcygeal teratoma is associated with a high recurrence rate.
items.a: Paediatric Radiology

items.c: Paget disease of the skull presents with lytic (osteolysis circumscripta) and sclerotic phases, with deafness being the most common clinical complication.
items.a: Skull base pathology

items.c: Think of PRES when encountering symmetric, subcortical T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the posterior hemispheres during a hypertensive emergency.
items.a: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome

items.t: Late gadolinium enhancement inversion recovery sequence
items.c: Subendocardial enhancement in a coronary territory is the hallmark of ischemic myocardial infarction on LGE-CMR.
items.a: Late gadolinium enhancement inversion recovery sequence

items.c: Distension of the esophagus is crucial during barium studies to differentiate varices from varicoid carcinoma.
items.a: Oesophagus

items.c: In sarcoidosis, look for perilymphatic nodules tracking along the fissures, bronchovascular bundles, and pleural surfaces.
items.a: Perilymphatic distribution

items.c: Duplicated inferior vena cava is frequently associated with renal anomalies like horseshoe or crossed fused ectopic kidneys.
items.a: Vascular

items.c: In a patient with acute flank pain and normal urinalysis, a disproportionately elevated LDH level should raise suspicion for renal infarction.
items.a: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)

items.c: Pneumatosis intestinalis is the pathognomonic radiological sign of necrotizing enterocolitis, appearing as linear lucencies in the bowel wall.
items.a: Pneumatosis intestinalis

items.c: The corona mortis is a high-risk vascular anastomosis that can cause life-threatening haemorrhage during pelvic surgery or trauma.
items.a: Pelvic vasculature

items.c: The Master Knot of Henry represents the site where the flexor digitorum longus tendon crosses over the flexor hallucis longus tendon.
items.a: Ankle

items.c: The presence of an intimomedial flap is the diagnostic hallmark differentiating aortic dissection from other acute aortic syndromes.
items.a: Aorta

items.c: SDHD mutations demonstrate a paternal parent-of-origin effect, meaning tumors typically develop only when the mutation is inherited from the father.
items.a: Familial Paraganglioma Syndrome Type 1 (PGL1)

items.c: Middle lobe and lingular bronchiectasis with nodules in an older woman suggests the nodular-bronchiectatic NTM pattern; imaging suggests it, microbiology confirms it.
items.a: Chest

items.c: Keep avascular necrosis as a differential, not a synonym: it needs a focal subchondral lesion, a double-line sign or collapse.
items.a: Hip

items.c: Multiple liver lesions alone cannot separate primary from metastatic neuroendocrine disease; with a known small-bowel primary, they are metastases.
items.a: Liver

items.c: Tumour thrombus needs internal enhancement, IVC expansion or continuity with a primary mass such as renal cell or hepatocellular carcinoma; a defect alone is indeterminate.
items.a: Vascular

items.c: Calcified neurocysticercosis is the end stage; a scolex belongs to the earlier vesicular stage, so do not assume one unless it is shown.
items.a: Neurocysticercosis

items.c: Absent kidneys alone do not separate metabolic from metastatic superscan; symmetry and appendicular plus calvarial uptake favour metabolic.
items.a: Bone scintigraphy

items.c: Humphrey runs in front of the PCL, Wrisberg behind it; do not mistake the ligament of Humphrey for a double PCL sign.
items.a: Knee

items.c: A unilateral hyperlucent hemithorax can come from the chest wall: check the pectoral muscles before blaming the lung.
items.a: Chest

items.c: Fine linear branching calcifications are highly suggestive of high-grade DCIS and warrant immediate tissue sampling.
items.a: Ductal carcinoma in situ

items.c: The trident sign on DWI is a pathognomonic finding for central pontine myelinolysis in osmotic demyelination syndrome.
items.a: Osmotic demyelination syndrome

items.c: New-onset dural arteriovenous fistulas should be suspected in patients with persistent ocular symptoms or worsening venous congestion following the successful endovascular treatment of a direct carotid-cavernous fistula.
items.a: Dural arteriovenous fistula

items.c: A well-defined, thin-walled, non-enhancing mesenteric cyst in an adult is most frequently a lymphangioma, which often requires surgical excision due to potential for mass effect or complications.
items.a: Mesenteric lymphangioma

items.c: In the peripheral zone, think DWI first; in the transition zone, think T2WI first.
items.a: Diffusion-weighted imaging

items.c: The Shenton line is the most sensitive early radiographic indicator of hip joint subluxation or dislocation in children.
items.a: Hilgenreiner line and Shenton line

items.c: The cerebriform pattern on MRI is a key diagnostic clue for inverted papilloma, reflecting its complex, infolded growth of squamous epithelium.
items.a: Cerebriform pattern

items.c: The crazy-paving pattern on HRCT combined with high-titer serum anti-GM-CSF antibodies is diagnostic of autoimmune PAP, often obviating the need for surgical biopsy.
items.a: Serum anti-GM-CSF autoantibody testing

items.c: The Oreo cookie sign on a lateral chest X-ray is a classic, highly specific indicator of pericardial effusion.
items.a: Oreo cookie sign

items.c: The distance between the tumor margin and the mesorectal fascia is the most critical prognostic factor for CRM positivity.
items.a: High-resolution T2-weighted turbo spin-echo sequence

items.c: The coffee bean sign on plain film is highly specific for sigmoid volvulus but lacks sensitivity in pediatric patients.
items.a: Coffee bean sign

items.t: Leiomyosarcoma of the inferior vena cava
items.c: A retroperitoneal mass with an imperceptible IVC wall and preserved lumen proximally and distally strongly suggests a primary venous leiomyosarcoma.
items.a: Leiomyosarcoma of the inferior vena cava

items.c: In a patient with a hypervascular spinal lesion and VHL syndrome, a cerebellar mass with high perfusion and no restricted diffusion is highly characteristic of a haemangioblastoma.
items.a: Cerebellar haemangioblastoma

items.t: Retention of barium in the colon is a reliable marker for the proximal extent of the aganglionic segment.
items.c: In suspected Hirschsprung disease, a 24-hour delayed abdominal radiograph showing retained barium is a strong predictor of the proximal extent of the aganglionic segment.
items.a: Retention of barium in the colon is a reliable marker for the proximal extent of the aganglionic segment.

items.c: Small bowel intussusception in a pediatric patient with mucocutaneous pigmentation should strongly raise suspicion for Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
items.a: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome polyposis

items.c: Always consider endovascular stenting following mechanical thrombectomy for symptomatic iliac vein compression to prevent chronic venous hypertension.
items.a: Stent placement across the compression

items.c: Rigler's triad is the pathognomonic radiological combination of pneumobilia, ectopic gallstone, and mechanical small bowel obstruction.
